Ran a Lean declaration-marker grep (theorem|lemma|def |structure|inductive|class |instance|abbrev|macro|elab|syntax|axiom) across all 46 `Provenance/**/*.lean` files: scores ranged from 6 (Algorithms/CompOp.lean) to 99 (HavingProbability.lean), a clean gradient with no zero-hit files.

Inspected `Provenance.lean` (root navigation file, 33189 bytes, 28 grep hits) in full: it is exclusively `import` statements (47 imports, each preceded by a one-line doc comment describing the imported module's role) followed by one large module-level doc comment (library overview, references, related-work discussion). Checked every one of the 28 grep hits by line number: all fall inside prose/doc-comment text (e.g. 'the algebraic structure ... together with general theorems about it', 'the bidirectional equisatisfiability theorem', 'the ℝ instance is also used as a counterexample') -- zero are actual `def`/`theorem`/`structure`/`instance` keyword declarations. Ran a `sorry`/`admit` sweep across all 46 files: two hits, both in `Provenance/AggQueryClosure.lean` and `Provenance/SemiringWithMonus.lean`; read each hit in context (lines 56/1576 of AggQueryClosure.lean, line 93 of SemiringWithMonus.lean) and confirmed both are prose uses of the English word 'admits' inside doc comments, not proof-placeholder tactics.

Spot-checked several mid/high-range files by size and hit count (e.g. Semirings/IntervalUnion.lean at 80 hits/72643 bytes, HavingComplexity.lean at 96 hits/91586 bytes) -- consistent structure of named theorems/lemmas/defs with doc comments and full tactic proofs, no anomalies.
